_comment: Cebuano function-word policy (tunatale-u8nz.4, 2026-09-25). 2026-10-14 (the user): the test is PICTUREABILITY, not part of speech. A root that can be pictured and extended with affixes is a vocab card, never a cloze; a cloze is for a word nothing can picture. So 'pos' is EMPTY and 'include' is the whole policy. The lemma table carries Wiktionary's UPOS, and that tags productive roots as closed-class: Cebuano gikan (from; mogikan 'depart', gigikanan 'origin') and uban (with; mouban) as ADP, duha (two) as DET; Tagalog mula and galing as ADP. A POS route would cloze them all. 'include' names the genuine difficulties for an English speaker: the case markers ang/sa/og, 'ug' (and), the personal-name markers si/ni/kang, the plural 'mga', the linker 'nga', and the second-position particles ba/pa/na/pud/sad/lang/ra/man/gyud/diay/kaha/unta. Tagalog's 'ng' and 'po' are deliberately absent: they are NOT Cebuano, and the style guide treats them as contamination. ORCHESTRATOR-DRAFTED, not native-checked (tunatale-u8nz.9). 2026-09-26: 'pero' (but) and 'para' (for) added on the user's call; they are CCONJ/ADP, which 'pos' would catch if Cebuano had an analyzer, so with none they must be named. 2026-09-28: 'ka' (the enclitic 'you') added on the user's call: it never starts a sentence, so it is drilled as a cloze; its free form 'ikaw' stays a picture card. Its UPOS stays PRON in closed_class.tsv. Same day, same rule: 'ko' (enclitic 'my / I'; free forms nako, ako). 2026-09-30: 'glosses' added: a curated gloss overrides the lesson gloss pass for a word whose meaning is a grammatical role. 'og' is the indefinite-object marker ('Nagdala ko og kape' = I brought (some) coffee); the LLM glossed it 'and', mistaking it for 'ug'. 'si' (personal-name topic marker) came back '[title]'. 'ni' is deliberately absent: it is also the short form of 'kini' (this), so only context can gloss it. 2026-10-14: 'kay' (because) and 'o' (or) added; they had reached the cloze route only by their CCONJ tag, and both have cloze cards in the live deck.
